group.title: Useful verbs
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To leave someone or something and never come back for them.
examples: The crew had to {abandon} the sinking ship.
wrong: They abandoned the old car by driving it every day.

words.meaning: To happen at the same time as something else.
examples: My birthday {coincides} with a national holiday this year.
wrong: The two events coincided: one was in May and the other in July.

words.meaning: To pay or give something to make up for a loss or damage.
examples: The airline {compensated} us for the lost luggage.
wrong: They compensated us by taking more money from us.

words.meaning: To hide something so others cannot see or know it.
examples: She tried to {conceal} her disappointment.
wrong: He concealed the note by pinning it to the front door.

words.meaning: To face a person or problem directly, often in a difficult way.
examples: She finally {confronted} her boss about the unfair rota.
wrong: He confronted the problem by pretending it wasn’t there.

words.meaning: To think about something carefully for a long time.
examples: He sat by the lake, {contemplating} his future.
wrong: She contemplated the offer without thinking about it once.

words.meaning: To make someone believe something that is not true.
examples: The ad {deceived} buyers about the price.
wrong: He deceived us by telling the complete truth.

words.meaning: To throw away something you no longer want.
examples: {Discard} the outer leaves of the lettuce.
wrong: I discarded the letter and kept it in a safe place.

words.meaning: To take someone’s attention away from what they are doing.
examples: The noise outside {distracted} me from my work.
wrong: The quiet room distracted me, so I focused better.

words.meaning: To suffer something painful or hard for a long time.
examples: The climbers {endured} freezing nights on the mountain.
wrong: She endured the pain by never feeling any.

words.meaning: To improve the quality or value of something.
examples: Good lighting can {enhance} a photograph.
wrong: The scratch enhanced the car by making it look worse.

words.meaning: To use someone unfairly for your own benefit.
examples: The factory {exploited} workers with long hours and low pay.
wrong: They exploited their staff by paying them fairly and well.

words.meaning: To live in a place.
examples: Rare birds {inhabit} these islands.
wrong: Nobody inhabits the house, and a family of five lives there.

words.meaning: To get involved in something that is not your business.
examples: Please don’t {interfere} in our argument.
wrong: He interfered by staying completely out of it.

words.meaning: To fail to give someone or something enough care.
examples: The garden was {neglected} and full of weeds.
wrong: She neglected her plants by watering them every day.

words.meaning: To fail to notice or think about something.
examples: The editor {overlooked} a spelling mistake on page one.
wrong: I overlooked the error, so I fixed it right away.

words.meaning: To continue doing something even when it is hard.
examples: If the pain {persists}, see a doctor.
wrong: The rain persisted, so it stopped after a minute.

words.meaning: To cause a reaction, often anger, on purpose.
examples: His rude comment {provoked} an angry reply.
wrong: She provoked him by speaking kindly and calmly.

words.meaning: To stop yourself from doing something.
examples: Please {refrain} from using your phone during the show.
wrong: He refrained from eating cake and ate three slices.

words.meaning: To keep or continue to have something.
examples: The town has {retained} its old charm.
wrong: The team retained the trophy by losing it to another club.

words.meaning: To throw or spread things over a wide area.
examples: He {scattered} seeds across the field.
wrong: The wind scattered the leaves into one neat pile.

words.meaning: To take hold of something quickly and firmly.
examples: She {seized} the rope just before she fell.
wrong: He seized the handle by letting go of it.

words.meaning: To try very hard to get or do something.
examples: We {strive} to answer every email within a day.
wrong: She strove for success by making no effort at all.

words.meaning: To be better or greater than someone or something.
examples: The results {surpassed} all our expectations.
wrong: Sales surpassed our goal by falling far below it.

words.meaning: To hold on to someone or something very tightly.
examples: The child {clung} to her mother’s hand in the crowd.
wrong: She clung to the rope by letting it go.

words.meaning: To almost fall after hitting your foot on something.
examples: I {stumbled} on the dark stairs.
wrong: She stumbled and walked perfectly smoothly.

words.meaning: To lift your shoulders to show you don’t know or care.
examples: When I asked where he’d been, he just {shrugged}.
wrong: He shrugged his shoulders by pushing them down firmly.

words.meaning: To run away from danger quickly.
examples: Families {fled} the village as the flood water rose.
wrong: They fled the fire by walking toward it.

words.meaning: To keep thinking or talking about something unpleasant for too long.
examples: Don’t {dwell} on your mistakes; learn from them.
wrong: She dwelled on the problem, so she never thought about it.

words.meaning: To expect something and prepare for it.
examples: We {anticipate} heavy traffic over the holiday.
wrong: Nobody anticipated the storm, so everyone was ready for it.

words.meaning: To know that something will happen before it does.
examples: No one could have {foreseen} the sudden change.
wrong: She foresaw the problem only after it happened.

words.meaning: To show or describe someone or something in a certain way.
examples: The film {portrays} the city as a lonely place.
wrong: The painting portrays a horse, but there is no horse in it.

words.meaning: To make pain or worry less bad.
examples: This cream will {relieve} the itching.
wrong: The medicine relieved the pain by making it much worse.

words.meaning: To find an answer to a problem or end a disagreement.
examples: The two sides {resolved} their dispute peacefully.
wrong: We resolved the problem, so it is still unsolved.

words.meaning: To make a real effort to deal with a difficult problem.
examples: The city plans to {tackle} its traffic problem.
wrong: He tackled the issue by avoiding it for years.

words.meaning: To accept something unpleasant without complaining.
examples: I can’t {tolerate} that loud music any longer.
wrong: She tolerates noise, so she complains about every sound.

words.meaning: To make something start to happen.
examples: Dust can {trigger} an allergy attack.
wrong: The smoke triggered the alarm, so it stayed silent.

words.meaning: To produce something useful, such as a crop or result.
examples: The research {yielded} some surprising results.
wrong: The trees yielded a large crop, but we found no fruit.

words.meaning: To accept a new idea or change eagerly.
examples: The school quickly {embraced} online learning.
wrong: The town embraced the new park by protesting against it.

words.meaning: To talk too proudly about what you have or can do.
examples: He’s always {boasting} about his expensive car.
wrong: She boasted about her prize by never mentioning it.
